source: v0 (literature) revised with taxonomy discovery on 60 papers (discovery_story.json)

archetype.title: Story archetype
archetype.q: Which recurring pitch does the paper use? Primary = what the abstract's first claim is; secondary only if the paper clearly chains two (e.g. a benchmark exposes a gap, then a fix).

benchmark-exposes-gap.name: New benchmark exposes a hidden failure
benchmark-exposes-gap.def: The paper builds a more realistic, composite or interactive evaluation and shows that models that look strong on existing benchmarks fail badly. A remedy is optional.
benchmark-exposes-gap.include_if: The main artifact is a benchmark or test protocol, and the headline finding is that current state-of-the-art systems perform much worse or differently than standard scores suggest.
benchmark-exposes-gap.exclude_if: The benchmark serves a domain that has no evaluation at all and the story is about enabling work there, not about overturning what looked like competence (use resource-for-underserved-domain). It is also excluded when the benchmark is a side component of a newly defined threat or task (use new-problem-or-threat).

resource-for-underserved-domain.name: Resource unlocks an underserved domain
resource-for-underserved-domain.def: The paper supplies a dataset, data-generation pipeline or expert-grounded evaluation for a domain where data or evaluation was missing, and shows that training or evaluating on it changes what is achievable.
resource-for-underserved-domain.include_if: The main contribution is a dataset or data framework, and the payoff is new capability, better generalization or the first reliable measurement in a specific domain.
resource-for-underserved-domain.exclude_if: The point is that existing top models break, not that the domain becomes possible to work on (use benchmark-exposes-gap).

new-problem-or-threat.name: Name a new problem or threat
new-problem-or-threat.def: The paper formalizes a problem, attack surface or pipeline step that prior work never posed, shows it matters in practice, and provides first measurements or baselines.
new-problem-or-threat.include_if: Before this paper the question was not asked at all (e.g., detecting unlearned models, cross-user poisoning, forget-set curation), and a task formulation is central.
new-problem-or-threat.exclude_if: The task is already known and the paper only measures it more realistically (use benchmark-exposes-gap). The paper is also excluded when it relaxes an assumption of an existing problem to get guarantees (use provable-reach-extended).

diagnose-then-fix.name: Diagnose the root cause, then fix it
diagnose-then-fix.def: Starting from a known shortfall, an analysis pinpoints a specific mechanistic cause, and a targeted method that removes that cause recovers the lost performance.
diagnose-then-fix.include_if: The paper has an explicit two-act structure: analysis names a culprit (credit misassignment, lazy reflection, spectral mismatch), then a method is designed against that culprit.
diagnose-then-fix.exclude_if: The analysis is a formal theory that defines the right quantity to optimize, rather than an empirical diagnosis of a failure (use principled-replacement). The paper is also excluded when the fix is mainly a way to get both sides of a trade-off and the diagnosis is minor (use tradeoff-dissolved).

tradeoff-dissolved.name: Get both sides of an assumed trade-off
tradeoff-dissolved.def: The field believes you must pick between two goods (speed vs. stability, fairness vs. truthfulness, flexibility vs. cost), and the paper's method achieves both.
tradeoff-dissolved.include_if: The 'seems' side states an explicit dichotomy or tension, and the 'really' side shows a design that keeps both properties.
tradeoff-dissolved.exclude_if: The belief is only that one component is required, with no second good at stake (use unnecessary-component). The paper is also excluded when the gain is reaching a scale or bound regime through structural assumptions (use provable-reach-extended).

unnecessary-component.name: The 'necessary' ingredient isn't
unnecessary-component.def: A component the field treats as required (a vision latent, graph priors, NMS, score conversion, a large LLM, anchors, many sequential rounds) is shown to be dispensable, and a simpler or cheaper pipeline matches or beats the standard one.
unnecessary-component.include_if: The headline claim is 'you don't need X', and the method demonstrates this by removing or replacing X.
unnecessary-component.exclude_if: Removing X is presented as getting both sides of a stated trade-off (use tradeoff-dissolved). The paper is also excluded when the main payoff is explaining why X seemed to work (use mechanism-revealed).

mechanism-revealed.name: Reveal what actually drives the behaviour
mechanism-revealed.def: Analysis uncovers the true mechanism behind an observed effect or behaviour (compression, not reasoning; alignment, not missing structure; decode-time, not prefill, subspaces). The finding is then often exploited cheaply.
mechanism-revealed.include_if: The core contribution is an explanatory or causal account of an existing model or phenomenon, and any method is a direct consequence of that account.
mechanism-revealed.exclude_if: The account is a formal theorem about rates or optimal quantities (use theory-overturns-intuition). The paper is also excluded when the analysis exists only to motivate fixing a specific failure (use diagnose-then-fix).

theory-overturns-intuition.name: Sharper theory overturns an intuition
theory-overturns-intuition.def: Rigorous analysis shows that a presumed rate, relation or sufficient condition is wrong: costs add rather than multiply, acceleration can hurt, KL-closeness does not imply similar representations, only covariance matters.
theory-overturns-intuition.include_if: The 'really' side is a theorem or bound contradicting a natural belief, and any algorithm mainly serves to realize or illustrate that bound.
theory-overturns-intuition.exclude_if: The theory is used to design a replacement for a heuristic, and the method is the headline (use principled-replacement). The paper is also excluded when the result is mainly reaching a new scale or setting (use provable-reach-extended).

controlled-comparison-overturns.name: Rigorous comparison overturns folk wisdom
controlled-comparison-overturns.def: Large, carefully controlled experiments or a predictive-fit methodology show that a widely held empirical ranking or recipe judgement is an artifact of unfair or small-scale comparison.
controlled-comparison-overturns.include_if: The main contribution is an experimental methodology (strict parity, scaling fits, large ablation sweeps) whose results reverse a conventional conclusion.
controlled-comparison-overturns.exclude_if: A new benchmark or task is the artifact (use benchmark-exposes-gap). The reversal is also excluded when it is proved rather than measured (use theory-overturns-intuition).

principled-replacement.name: Principled theory replaces a heuristic
principled-replacement.def: The paper shows that a heuristic practice is suboptimal or unanalyzed and replaces it with a method derived from theory (information theory, extreme-value tails, geometry), backed by guarantees.
principled-replacement.include_if: The pitch is 'heuristic → principled with guarantees': the heuristic is shown to be biased or unexplained, and the new method comes with theorems.
principled-replacement.exclude_if: The theorem itself, not the method, is the headline (use theory-overturns-intuition). The paper is also excluded when the motivation is an empirical diagnosis of a failure (use diagnose-then-fix).

provable-reach-extended.name: Extend guarantees or scale to a harder regime
provable-reach-extended.def: Results previously limited to small, exact-access or whole-stream settings are carried to million-node graphs, time-decay streams, black-box lower levels or polylogarithmic memory. This is usually done by exploiting structure or weaker assumptions.
provable-reach-extended.include_if: The 'seems' side is 'infeasible, or only known under assumption A', and the 'really' side is a provable algorithm that works in the harder regime.
provable-reach-extended.exclude_if: Two competing goods are both obtained, with no regime change (use tradeoff-dissolved). The paper is also excluded when the result says an existing rate or intuition is wrong (use theory-overturns-intuition).

decompose-the-monolith.name: Decompose what was treated as one thing
decompose-the-monolith.def: A signal, state or attribution treated as a single object is split into components (line-level rewards, spatial vs. memory contributions, action-responsive vs. exogenous state), and modelling each separately fixes the problem.
decompose-the-monolith.include_if: The key move is a decomposition, and the method directly operates on the parts.
decompose-the-monolith.exclude_if: The decomposition only diagnoses a failure that a different mechanism then fixes (use diagnose-then-fix). The paper is also excluded when the split serves a benchmark's failure analysis (use benchmark-exposes-gap).

unification.name: Unify scattered methods as one family
unification.def: Methods seen as separate are shown to be instances or approximations of one framework, which explains them and yields new variants, libraries or design freedom.
unification.include_if: The 'seems' side is 'A and B are different', and the 'really' side is a common derivation or framework within the same field.
unification.exclude_if: The unifying lens is imported from a different discipline, and the problem is recast as that field's problem (use cross-field-reframe).

cross-field-reframe.name: Recast the problem in another field's terms
cross-field-reframe.def: The paper argues that an ML problem is really an instance of a mature problem from another area (probabilistic programming, systems security, KV-cache reconciliation) and imports that area's abstractions to solve it.
cross-field-reframe.include_if: The pitch is 'X is really a Y problem', and the contribution is the formulation plus a system or principles imported from Y.
cross-field-reframe.exclude_if: Methods within the same field are merged, with no import from another discipline (use unification).

niche.title: Why it was needed
niche.q: Why is the paper needed? (the gap the introduction sets up)

unexplored-gap.name: Unexplored gap
unexplored-gap.def: an aspect, setting or regime nobody has addressed (includes applying known ideas to a new setting)

missing-evaluation.name: Missing evaluation
missing-evaluation.def: claims in the field lack proper evidence, measurement or benchmark

prior-shortfall.name: Prior methods fall short
prior-shortfall.def: existing methods are not accurate or capable enough

prior-cost.name: Prior methods cost too much
prior-cost.def: existing methods are too slow, expensive or data-hungry; use only if cost is the headline, not a side benefit

prior-fragility.name: Prior methods are fragile
prior-fragility.def: existing methods break under shift, noise, attack or scale

prior-assumption.name: Prior methods assume too much
prior-assumption.def: existing methods rely on assumptions that are too strong or unrealistic

conflicting-evidence.name: Conflicting evidence
conflicting-evidence.def: results or explanations in the literature disagree

new-problem.name: A new problem
new-problem.def: a task, threat or capability that had not been posed before

method.name: Method
method.def: a new model, algorithm, objective or training recipe

dataset-benchmark.name: Dataset benchmark
dataset-benchmark.def: a dataset, benchmark or evaluation protocol

task-formulation.name: Task formulation
task-formulation.def: a new problem formulation or task definition

explanation.name: Explanation
explanation.def: an explanation or mechanism for an observed behaviour

characterization.name: Characterization
characterization.def: a systematic characterization, e.g. scaling laws or large-scale study

analysis-of-existing.name: Analysis of existing
analysis-of-existing.def: an analysis or re-evaluation of existing methods

negative-result.name: Negative result
negative-result.def: showing something does not work or does not hold

position-survey.name: Position or survey
position-survey.def: an argument, perspective or systematization of a field

insight_origin.title: Where the insight comes from
insight_origin.q: Where does the key insight come from?

analogy.name: Analogy
analogy.def: borrowed from another field or problem

first-principles.name: First principles
first-principles.def: derived from theory or first principles

reframing.name: Reframing
reframing.def: recasting the problem as a known, solved problem

evidence.title: Evidence
evidence.q: What kinds of evidence carry the paper's main claim?

benchmark-comparison.name: Benchmark comparison
benchmark-comparison.def: head-to-head results against baselines on benchmarks

controlled-synthetic.name: Controlled synthetic
controlled-synthetic.def: toy or synthetic settings with known ground truth

large-scale-study.name: Large scale study
large-scale-study.def: large sweeps or measurements across many models/settings

existence-demo.name: Existence demo
existence-demo.def: a demonstration that something can be done at all

changes_from_v0: arc labels replaced by data-driven archetypes (v0 arcs overlapped: seems-necessary vs tradeoff-resolved vs impossible-feasible were co-assigned on 10 of 60 papers)
niche merged: overlooked-aspect + underexplored-setting + new-setting-transfer -> unexplored-gap; assumption-challenged moved to archetypes
challenged belief now requires an explicit, quoted statement of a widely held belief (v0 filled it for 56 of 60 papers)
